## Paper 1 · Session 02 · News sentiment and stock returns {.center .scrollable}

## The paper, and its question {.scrollable}

**Fraiberger, Lee, Puy & Ranciere (2021)**, *Media sentiment and international asset prices*,
Journal of International Economics · [article](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jinteco.2021.103526)

The authors turn millions of Reuters articles about 25 countries into a **daily news-sentiment
index**: the share of positive words minus the share of negative ones, standardised within each
country. They ask whether a better-than-usual news day predicts higher stock returns.

> **Does a one-standard-deviation rise in a country's news sentiment go with higher stock returns
> there the next day, once past returns, volume, volatility and global risk are held fixed?**

## The data, and the simple model {.scrollable}

**One row = one country-day**, weekends included: 246,550 rows; **135,082** have a return and the
three predictors.

## What you should find {.scrollable}

| | sentiment coefficient | in words |
|---|---|---|
| Step 4 · OLS, sentiment only | 0.072 | +0.07 points of return per sd |
| Step 5 · OLS, + return and VIX | 0.067 | the same, holding them fixed |
| Step 6 · logit, odds ratio | 1.069 | odds of an up day 7% higher per sd |
| Step 7 · P(up day) | 0.502 → 0.535 | from a bad to a good news day |
| **Paper**, 8 lags of everything | **0.049** | with country effects and extreme days |

::: {.check}
Very significant, very small: with 135,082 rows the p-value is near zero, but $R^2 \approx 0.001$.
The paper's richer controls bring the slope from 0.07 down to 0.05.
:::

## What it does not license {.scrollable}

::: {.tight}
- **No causal claim.** The same event can move both the news and the market; a one-day lag does not
  rule that out.
- **No trading rule.** 0.07 points a day is far below a daily return spread of 1.9 points — before costs.
- **No claim to have reproduced the paper.** Our model is deliberately simpler; its slope is not theirs.
:::

::: {.muted}
Pitfall: the panel has **calendar** days. Sentiment exists on Sundays; returns do not.
:::
